atlasGallery.author: Alex Kesin (project owner)
atlasGallery.title: DSC08767 · Absalom's monument, face with the breach
atlasGallery.alt: Absalom's monument in afternoon sun: the lower cube with engaged columns and a ragged hole above them, the attic, drum and cone; a pedimented doorway behind it at left and a cut rock scarp at right.
atlasGallery.caption: The face of Absalom's monument in afternoon sun. A ragged hole goes through the face above the columns. Above the cube are the attic, the drum and the cone. A pedimented doorway with a grille shows behind the monument at left (the Jehoshaphat tomb doorway; background only, no frieze detail). A cut rock scarp is at right. Gravel ground runs up to the stepped base. INFERENCE: west face, because the Jehoshaphat doorway, which lies NE, shows behind at left. No GPS, no compass heading, no scale object. 1616 px reduced copy.
atlasGallery.relevance: Entry 48 asks only for the monument's west side. Kloner–Zissu (p. 142) put the original entrance in the south wall and call the western opening a later breach. Photos record shape and facing; they date nothing.

atlasGallery.author: Alex Kesin (project owner)
atlasGallery.title: DSC08770 · Absalom's monument, corner view of cube, attic and drum
atlasGallery.alt: Low corner view of Absalom's monument: two faces of the cube with engaged columns and a decorated frieze, the attic above and the drum with a rope moulding; a pine tree behind.
atlasGallery.caption: Low view at a corner of the monument. Two faces of the lower cube show engaged columns with Ionic capitals and a frieze of discs between upright bands. Above are the cornice, the plain attic and the drum with a rope moulding; the top of the cone shows. The face at right has the hole above its columns. The view is too low and too oblique to count the courses above the cube. No GPS, no compass heading, no scale object. 1616 px reduced copy.
atlasGallery.relevance: Entry 2: Absalom's lower body is rock-cut, so it supplies no built third course (Kloner–Zissu 2003 pp. 142, 146). The parts above the cube show here, but their courses cannot be counted. Photos record shape; they date nothing.

records.subject: close view of the face with the barred breach

atlasGallery.author: Alex Kesin (project owner)
atlasGallery.title: DSC08773 · Absalom's monument, the barred breach
atlasGallery.alt: View up the face of Absalom's monument: engaged columns with Ionic capitals under a frieze and cornice, and a ragged hole in the face closed by vertical iron bars.
atlasGallery.caption: Close view up the face with the hole. The hole is ragged, and vertical iron bars close it. Engaged columns with Ionic capitals carry a decorated frieze and a cornice; the attic and the rope moulding of the drum show above. A modern wall with a railing is at left. The photo does not show what is behind the bars. INFERENCE: this is the west face, the same face as in DSC08767. No GPS, no compass heading, no scale object. 1616 px reduced copy.
atlasGallery.relevance: Entry 48: Kloner–Zissu (p. 142) call the western opening a later breach. The photo shows its present form only; it dates nothing.

atlasGallery.author: Alex Kesin (project owner)
atlasGallery.title: DSC08791 · Bene Ḥezir tomb façade, high in the scarp
atlasGallery.alt: A tall rock scarp at right with the columned porch of the Bene Ḥezir tomb high up behind a metal railing; a terraced slope with cypresses and olive trees at left.
atlasGallery.caption: View up the rock scarp from below. High in the scarp is the porch of the Bene Ḥezir tomb: columns under a frieze, with a metal railing and a sign panel in front. The façade inscription is not legible at this distance or resolution. Small rectangular recesses show lower in the rock face. A terraced slope with cypresses and olive trees is at left. No GPS, no compass heading, no scale object. 1616 px reduced copy.
atlasGallery.relevance: Entry 51: Bene Ḥezir is the only recorded pillared-porch tomb near the site (Kloner–Zissu pp. 143–146). The shot-list aim, a legible façade inscription, was not met in this set. Photos record shape; they date nothing.

atlasGallery.author: Alex Kesin (project owner)
atlasGallery.title: DSC08812 · Zechariah's monument, front
atlasGallery.alt: Front of Zechariah's monument: a cube with Ionic engaged columns, a cornice and a pyramid roof, standing in a rock cutting with rock walls at both sides; a metal stair at left.
atlasGallery.caption: The front of the monument. The cube stands in a cutting, with cut rock close at both sides. Engaged columns and corner pilasters carry Ionic capitals; above are a cornice and a pyramid roof. A modern metal stair is at left. Dry-stone walls are on the slope at right. A blue painted mark is on the rock under the base. No GPS, no compass heading, no scale object. 1616 px reduced copy.
atlasGallery.relevance: Entry 2: Zechariah's monument is monolithic, so it supplies no built third course (Kloner–Zissu 2003 pp. 142, 146). Photos record shape and facing; they date nothing.

atlasGallery.author: Alex Kesin (project owner)
atlasGallery.title: DSC08818 · Absalom's monument, drum and cone from above
atlasGallery.alt: The drum and concave cone of Absalom's monument seen from above behind a metal fence, with a dark gap in the drum and the Old City wall and olive terraces behind.
atlasGallery.caption: The top of the monument seen from above, from behind a metal fence. The drum is round, with rope mouldings. The cone is concave and ends in a short shaft with a rope ring. Joints between stones show in the drum and the cone. A dark gap opens in the drum on the side toward the camera. Behind are the Old City wall and terraces with olive trees. INFERENCE: the camera looks about west, because the Old City wall is on the west side of the valley. No GPS, no compass heading, no scale object. 1616 px reduced copy.
atlasGallery.relevance: Entry 2: Absalom's lower body is rock-cut (Kloner–Zissu 2003 pp. 142, 146); this shows the parts above it. No frame in this set is square-on enough to count their courses reliably. Photos record shape and facing; they date nothing.

atlasGallery.author: Alex Kesin (project owner)
atlasGallery.title: IMG_9844 at 50 s · Zechariah's monument, engraved letters
atlasGallery.alt: View up two engaged columns of Zechariah's monument with Ionic capitals under the cornice; several groups of engraved letters are cut into a column shaft and the flat surface beside it.
atlasGallery.caption: Video frame looking up at two engaged columns with Ionic capitals under the cornice. Several groups of engraved letters are cut into one column shaft and into the flat surface at right. They are clearer here than in the camera photos DSC08804, 08805 and 08810, but this project has not read or dated them. Frame at 50 s of the owner's iPhone 15 video IMG_9844 (1920 × 1080 px). The video records only its start position (±12.5 m) and no compass heading; no scale object.
atlasGallery.relevance: Entry 2 discusses this monument. The letters are an edition and dating question for the published inscriptions, not a test in this project. Photos record shape; they date nothing.
